transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2025-06-18
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: 48 minutes (recorded)
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Sara Lopez (Acme Head of ML), Tom Nguyen (Acme Platform Lead), Jules Park (Acme SRE)

Summary:
Quick scoping call to align on POC success criteria, workload sizing and traffic modelling for a Redwood Dedicated pilot. Focus on QPS, concurrency, token distributions, latency SLOs and benchmark plan + timeline.

Topics:
- Production workload profile (QPS, spikes, concurrency)
- Input/output token distribution and prompt templates
- Benchmark parameters and metrics (p50/p95 latency, error rates, cost per 1k tokens)
- POC timeline and deliverables

-- Transcript --
[00:00] Alex: hey everyone thanks for joining, uh quick intro, i'm alex from redwood, and ravi's our se, we'll run through the scoping for the poc. how's everyone doing?
[00:18] Sara: good, thanks. we got a busy day. trying to get this POC scoped so we can move to procurement.
[00:26] Tom: yea, timeline is the hurry - procurement wants a 2 week pilot then sizing.
[00:33] Ravi: cool, can we start with current traffic? sara or tom can you summarize qps and concurrency?
[00:41] Tom: sure. baseline is about 1200 requests per hour during peak day, so roughly 0.33 rps average but we get bursts. peak burst qps hits about 18 qps for short windows, maybe 30-60s. concurrent open sessions typically 40-60 during promo events.
[01:05] Alex: ok, so steady-state low but bursty. for POC do you want us to target your peak bursts or typical daily traffic?
[01:13] Sara: both. success criteria: meet p95 latency < 350ms for generation + <1% error at our 95th token-length distribution, and cost should be under our internal threshold (we'll share). we also want determinism for inference outputs, and audit logs.
[01:30] Ravi: that's helpful. Can you share token histograms? average input token length?
[01:36] Sara: yes, average user prompt ~85 tokens, mean output ~140 tokens. 90th percentile output is ~420 tokens (we have long receipts and post-purchase summaries). There's a long tail.
[01:53] Tom: also note we do reranking flows - small inputs, multiple candidates (n=5) at ~2k qps internal during batch jobs — not user-facing but important for nightly jobs.
[02:07] Alex: good — that suggests we need separate profiles: low-latency chat path for interactive flows and high-throughput batching for rerank. does that match?
[02:16] Sara: yes exactly.
[02:20] Ravi: for modeling the workload we'll want: qps distribution over 24h, concurrency histograms, token length distributions for in/out, and any batching behavior client-side. Also, any SLO windows (promo events).
[02:33] Tom: i'll provide 14 days of logs with request timestamps and token counts. we'll scrub pids and user ids.
[02:39] Alex: excellent. on the redwood side we typically model two traffic shapes: interactive (avg qps ~1-5, bursts to 20-30, concurrency 10-60) and batch/rerank (high qps over short window, concurrent CPU/GPU utilization). we use that to size dedicated pools and choose quantization profiles.
[02:58] Sara: how do you recommend handling the 420-token tail? it's killing our latency sometimes.
[03:04] Ravi: a few options: 1) route long outputs to a slower higher-throughput instance (cheaper quantized model) with relaxed p95 SLO, 2) enforce truncation or progressive generation w/streaming so perceived latency is lower, 3) increase dedicated capacity during promo windows. tradeoffs are cost vs latency/quality.
[03:24] Alex: also, pre-cache common prefixes for receipts could save tokens. Do you have repeated templates?
[03:30] Sara: yes, 30% of outputs reuse a templated header. we can prefill.
[03:35] Tom: for the rerank nightly batch, we expect upwards of 50k candidates processed per hour, that's high throughput but tolerant of higher latency.
[03:44] Ravi: ok we'll model rerank as throughput job with less strict p95, prioritize cost efficiency.
[03:50] Alex: let's talk concrete benchmark targets for the POC: recommend 48-hour run with mixed workload: 1) interactive profile ramping to 20 qps bursts, mean input 85 tokens mean output 140 tokens, sustained concurrency ~40; 2) one 1-hour rerank sweep at simulated 2k qps for small inputs; 3) synthetic long-tail generation at p99 output length to validate fallback routing. metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, throughput, success/error rate, token cost, and resource utilization (GPU mem, batch sizes). Sound reasonable?
[04:27] Sara: yes that seems right. timeline?
[04:30] Alex: propose: this week - customer sends logs + confirm success criteria. next week - Redwood runs lab benchmark using sanitized logs and baseline models (open-llama / opt variants), we produce a benchmark report by end of next week. then 2-week pilot on dedicated capacity with canary traffic and monitoring. so total ~3-4 weeks to go from scoping to pilot.
[04:53] Tom: procurement needs a pricing ballpark earlier. can you send a pricing matrix?
[04:57] Alex: yes we'll share estimated cost per 1M tokens for the model variants and a dedicated pool estimate.
[05:03] Ravi: on technical setup, for private data concerns do you need VPC or dedicated?
[05:08] Sara: we need VPC plus KMS integration for keys; SOC2 and audit logs are required.
[05:13] Alex: we support that on Redwood Private; we can provide SOC2 artifacts and audit log retention options. we'll include the security pack in the docs.
[05:21] Jules: are there special networking requirements? we run in GCP only.
[05:25] Ravi: we can provision in GCP region and set up a peering / private link. There may be egress rules. we'll capture specifics in the security doc.
[05:34] Tom: about the load generation - do you need us to provide real prompts or can you synthesize from token histograms?
[05:40] Alex: both. real prompts better for quality/regression checks; histograms good for driving token-length distributions. for rerank we'll need candidate set shapes.
[05:48] Sara: one more question on observability - can you show per-route token cost and p95 dashboards?
[05:53] Ravi: yes Redwood Console gives per-route cost breakdown, token breakdown and tracing hooks. we'll attach screenshots. sometimes the transcription spells things weird - our console shows KV cache as “K-V cash” in older notes, so ignore that in older doc.
[06:08] Tom: haha noted.
[06:10] Alex: any blockers from your side for the logs or security?
[06:13] Sara: we need legal to sign a DPA but that shouldn't block the bench.
[06:17] Tom: procurement wants an official statement of work for the pilot.
[06:20] Alex: we'll draft an SOW and share along with pricing.
[06:24] Ravi: on benchmarks, expected model choices? we typically test a smaller quantized open model and a medium-sized variant to compare latency/quality tradeoffs; we can also test a Redwood-verified optimized variant. which model families do you prefer?
[06:38] Sara: open to both; we want to compare to our current hosted provider (we won't name them on the call) but quality parity is important.
[06:46] Alex: ok. to recap next steps: redwood shares pricing, benchmark script, and security artifacts; acme sends 14 days of logs and confirms success criteria; schedule benchmark kickoff next week.
[06:58] Sara: sounds good. thanks Alex and Ravi.
[07:02] Alex: thanks everyone. we'll follow up with a calendar invite for the kickoff and send the data template.
[07:07] Tom: thanks. bye.

Notes on transcription quality: occasional mis-attributions and ASR errors (proper nouns occasionally mangled), some filler words retained.

End of transcript.
